chapter: Larry in Chicago and New York
title: Father's reluctance; Larry returns from the New York flop and leaves again with Tom Brown
summary: Harry's father wanted the boys to paint; after the Brown band flopped in Chicago and New York, Larry returned, then left again after Tom Brown persuaded the parents, and Larry ended up with Nick LaRocca.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I think you were a band. You folks didn't mind you learning music then, I guess, as long as Larry was in it too.
Well, my dad really didn't want us to learn. He wanted us to work, paint, you know. He'd paint us because he figured if we were out, which I'd stay out pretty late some nights playing.

Then wouldn't want to get up in the morning to go to work and Larry too. Because after Larry came back from the first trip, he went to Chicago, they flopped, and they went to New York and flopped. They had Ray Lopez on cornet then. We interviewed him in California. Tom Brown's man from Dixieland and Anilay Cano was on bass and piano. And Billy Lambeth on drums.
I never knew him. He was on bass and piano.

Yeah. And I understand they flopped. And when Larry came back home, my dad said, well, that's the end of it. Just, well, throw that thing away and come to work and forget the music. So Larry said, well, all right. And he went to work with my dad. One afternoon, Tom Brown came to the house. And he said, well, I'm going to go to work with him. So Larry told my dad, he looked out, he said, it's Tom Brown out there. So my dad said, I'll go talk to him. So he went out and he said, Tommy said, now look, Brown, if you're coming here to get this boy to go away again, you just won't forget about it. Now he's back working and I don't want him to go up there and starve. So Tom said, oh no, Mr. Shields, this is the real McCoy this time. He said, here it is, here. You read this telegram and we're going to make so much. And this is it now. Larry was talking to my mother at the time in the kitchen. Of course, you know, the mother liked, she said. Our dad come in, Tom came in with him. Tom was very insistent. I'm glad he was at the time. So Tom started talking to my mother. My mother said, well, if the boy wants to go, he's not happy painting. He wants to play music. Let him go. So she said, you sure you want to go? Larry said, yes, I want to go. All right. My dad said, well, okay. Your mother says, let you go. Go ahead. So he did, but something happened in Chicago. He left Brown's band. And I think he swapped jobs with Gussie Miller.
What's that? Gussie Miller was very good.

Gussie can tell you that. I heard that. Somebody told me that. And he went to work at White City and Gussie Miller went to work with Tom Brown at the College Inn, I think it was, in Chicago. And then Larry didn't like working with this big band out in White City. And just about that time, Yellow quit Nick LaRocca. And so they asked Larry to join the band. So Larry said, well, Yellow quit. All right. He said, I don't like this outfit I'm with now. No. So Larry joined Nick then. And then he left the casino garden and said, what in New York? You got to make it money.
